title: Add the architecture
body: T23 from Factory v0: docs/architecture.md, the third planning document. It turns docs/product-brief.md and docs/requirements.md into numbered architecture decisions (AD-01 onwards), components, request flow, module layout, dependencies, testing approach, and a coverage table for every requirement. Later planning steps (data model, API and security decisions, acceptance tests, task graph) cite the AD IDs.

change.prompt:
Write docs/architecture.md, the architecture for this app, from docs/product-brief.md and docs/requirements.md. Create only docs/architecture.md. Do not change any other file, do not install packages, and do not write code.

This is the third planning document. The next steps are the data model, the API and security decisions, the acceptance tests, and a task graph of independent build tasks. They cite this document's decisions by ID, so the IDs and their format matter. Where the requirements' Decisions section and the brief differ, the requirements win: projects are shared between an owner and members, accounts use an email address and a password, and changes reach other members on their next page load, not live.

Facts about where this app is built and tested, which you cannot see from the repository:
- The scaffold is Next.js 16.3.6 with the App Router, React 19.2, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, ESLint 9, and Vitest 5 with jsdom. It runs on Node 24 with npm 11.16. Keep all of it.
- CI is GitHub Actions on ubuntu-24.04. It runs npm ci, npm run lint, npm run build, and npm test, with no database service and no secrets.
- Build tasks run on a factory worker: an Amazon Linux 2023 machine with no Docker and no browsers. Its checks also run npm ci, lint, build, and test.
- npm 11.16 skips a package's install scripts unless package.json approves them in allowScripts. A dependency that needs an install script, such as a native module that downloads or compiles a binary, must say so under Dependencies.
- Node 24 has a built-in SQLite module, node:sqlite, that works without a flag.

Calls already made, so write them in as decisions:
- Persistence is SQLite in a local file, because CI and the worker have no database service. Tests use a fresh database of their own.
- Tests run in Vitest through npm test. There are no browser end-to-end tests, because the worker has no browsers. Acceptance tests check observable behaviour through server-side functions and rendered components (NFR-05).
- The app needs no hosted service at runtime. Deployment and hosting are out of scope for this document, so raise them as an open question.

Decide the rest, the simplest option that meets the requirements, and give a short reason for each: the SQLite driver and data-access layer; a maintained auth library, or a small session implementation of your own, for email and password sign-in; Server Actions or Route Handlers for changes; where sign-in and access checks sit, so that access control is enforced where data is read and changed (NFR-01), not only in the interface; how validation works (NFR-02); and the module layout. Before you decide, read the relevant guides in node_modules/next/dist/docs/, which setup has installed: at least 01-app/02-guides/authentication.md, 01-app/01-getting-started/07-mutating-data.md, and 01-app/01-getting-started/16-proxy.md. Use this Next.js version's names and conventions. You may check a package with npm view, but do not install anything.

Leave the details to the later steps. Name the main entities and which part of the app owns them, but leave tables, columns, and indexes to the data model step. Leave session lifetime, cookie settings, password hashing parameters, and rate limiting to the security step.

Rules:
- Do not widen the scope beyond the requirements. Do not read or cite the vendored skills in .agents/ or .claude/.
- Outside Constraints, Out of scope, and Open questions, do not name any hosted database or database server, cloud or hosting service, container tool, browser test tool, GraphQL or tRPC, live transport such as WebSockets or server-sent events, or sign-in method other than email and password (such as passkeys, magic links, SSO, OAuth, or MFA).
- Plain English and short sentences, 1200 to 3500 words. No marketing language, no placeholders (TBD, TODO, FIXME, lorem), and no emoji.

Use exactly these headings in this order, with no other level-1 or level-2 headings, and put a blank line after every heading:

# Architecture: Agent Factory Benchmark
## Overview: two or three sentences on what the app is and that later planning documents cite decisions by ID.
## Constraints: the facts above that shape the design, including Node 24, CI, and the Amazon Linux 2023 worker.
## Decisions: a bulleted list of 6 to 15 decisions.
## Components: the main parts of the app and what each one owns, including the main entities.
## Request flow: what happens from a request to the database and back for a page view and for a change, including where the session is read and where access is checked. Cite NFR-01.
## Module layout: a fenced code block with the planned directory tree, starting from app/, then a sentence or two on it.
## Dependencies: a table with the columns Package, Purpose, and Decision, one row per new npm package, at most 8. Write each package name alone in backticks in the Package column, and cite the AD ID that needs it in the Decision column. Only list packages that exist on npm and are not already in package.json. If there are none, write one sentence saying so instead of a table.
## Testing: how the requirements are tested with Vitest through npm test, including how each test gets its own database and how signed-in users are simulated. Cite NFR-05.
## Requirement coverage: one Markdown table with the columns Requirements, Components, and Decisions. Group related requirements into rows, and list every FR and NFR ID from docs/requirements.md individually (for example FR-01, FR-02, FR-03, not FR-01 to FR-03), each exactly once. Every row cites at least one AD ID.
## Out of scope: what this document does not decide, including deployment and hosting.
## Assumptions: a bulleted list of the smaller choices this document makes that nobody has confirmed, at least 2.
## Open questions: 1 to 6 questions for the operator's review.

The heading lines themselves are only the text before the colon, for example "## Overview".

Decisions:
- One bullet per decision, on one line, in the form: - **AD-01** Persistence is SQLite in a local file. CI and the worker have no database service. (FR-12, NFR-06)
- Number them AD-01, AD-02, and so on, in order with no gaps and always two digits.
- Each decision cites, in parentheses at the end, the IDs of the requirements it serves.
- Only cite FR, NFR, and AD IDs that exist.

Open questions: each bullet is one line. It starts with the IDs of the decisions or requirements its answer would change, in parentheses, and ends with a question mark.

When you finish, run every verify command listed below yourself, and fix whatever fails.

verify:
python3 -c 'import re, json, subprocess; t = open("docs/architecture.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); R = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None; fence = False; H = []
for i, l in enumerate(R):
    if l.startswith("```"): fence = not fence
    if not fence and re.match(r"#{1,6} ", l): H.append(i)
    if not fence and l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
want = ["# Architecture: Agent Factory Benchmark", "## Overview", "## Constraints", "## Decisions", "## Components", "## Request flow", "## Module layout", "## Dependencies", "## Testing", "## Requirement coverage", "## Out of scope", "## Assumptions", "## Open questions"]
assert R[0] == want[0], "title"
heads = [R[i] for i in H if re.match(r"#{1,2} ", R[i])]; assert heads == want, heads
bad = [R[i] for i in H if i + 1 >= len(R) or R[i + 1] != ""]; assert not bad, ("no blank line after", bad)
n = len(t.split()); assert 1200 <= n <= 3500, f"{n} words"
assert not re.search(r"\b(TBD|TODO|FIXME)\b", t) and "lorem" not in t.lower(), "placeholder"
assert not re.search("[\U0001F300-\U0001FAFF\u2600-\u27BF]", t), "emoji"
'

python3 -c 'import re, json, subprocess; t = open("docs/architecture.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); R = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None; fence = False; H = []
for i, l in enumerate(R):
    if l.startswith("```"): fence = not fence
    if not fence and re.match(r"#{1,6} ", l): H.append(i)
    if not fence and l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
req = set(re.findall(r"^- \*\*(N?FR-\d{2})\*\* ", open("docs/requirements.md", encoding="utf-8").read(), re.M)); assert len(req) >= 24, len(req)
ab = bullets("Decisions")
assert all(re.match(r"- \*\*AD-\d{2}\*\* \S", l) for l in ab), [l for l in ab if not re.match(r"- \*\*AD-\d{2}\*\* \S", l)]
a = [l[4:9] for l in ab]; assert 6 <= len(a) <= 15 and a == [f"AD-{i:02d}" for i in range(1, len(a) + 1)], a
assert all(re.search(r"\bN?FR-\d{2}\b", l) for l in ab), ("each decision cites a requirement", [l[:40] for l in ab if not re.search(r"\bN?FR-\d{2}\b", l)])
used = set(re.findall(r"\bN?FR-\d+\b", t)); assert used <= req, ("unknown requirement IDs", sorted(used - req))
ads = set(re.findall(r"\bAD-\d+\b", t)); assert ads <= set(a), ("unknown decision IDs", sorted(ads - set(a)))
rows = [[c.strip() for c in l.strip().strip("|").split("|")] for l in sec["Requirement coverage"] if l.startswith("|") and re.search(r"\bN?FR-\d{2}\b", l)]
cov = {x for r in rows for x in re.findall(r"\bN?FR-\d{2}\b", r[0])}; assert cov == req, ("coverage table must list every requirement ID", sorted(req - cov))
assert all(len(r) == 3 and re.search(r"\bAD-\d{2}\b", r[2]) for r in rows), ("each coverage row names a decision", [r[0] for r in rows if len(r) != 3 or not re.search(r"\bAD-\d{2}\b", r[2])])
'

python3 -c 'import re, json, subprocess; t = open("docs/architecture.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); R = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None; fence = False; H = []
for i, l in enumerate(R):
    if l.startswith("```"): fence = not fence
    if not fence and re.match(r"#{1,6} ", l): H.append(i)
    if not fence and l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
d = body("Decisions")
for w in [r"\bsqlite\b", r"\bsessions?\b", r"\bpasswords?\b", r"\bvitest\b", r"server actions?|server functions?|route handlers?"]: assert re.search(w, d, re.I), ("decisions", w)
c = body("Constraints"); assert re.search(r"node(\.js)? 24", c, re.I) and re.search(r"amazon linux", c, re.I), "constraints"
assert "NFR-01" in body("Request flow"), "request flow cites NFR-01"
x = body("Testing"); assert "npm test" in x and "NFR-05" in x, "testing"
m = body("Module layout"); assert m.count("```") >= 2 and "app/" in m, "module layout"
assert re.search(r"deploy|hosting", body("Out of scope") + body("Open questions"), re.I), "deployment"
assert len(bullets("Assumptions")) >= 2, "assumptions"
q = bullets("Open questions"); assert 1 <= len(q) <= 6 and all(l.rstrip().endswith("?") and re.search(r"\b(N?FR|AD)-\d{2}\b", l) for l in q), q
'

python3 -c 'import re, json, subprocess; t = open("docs/architecture.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); R = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None; fence = False; H = []
for i, l in enumerate(R):
    if l.startswith("```"): fence = not fence
    if not fence and re.match(r"#{1,6} ", l): H.append(i)
    if not fence and l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
x = "\n".join(l for s, ls in sec.items() if s not in ("Constraints", "Out of scope", "Open questions") for l in ls)
bad = r"\b(postgres(ql)?|mysql|mariadb|dynamo(db)?|mongo(db)?|supabase|firebase|redis|cognito|auth0|clerk|lambda|fargate|ecs|eks|amplify|s3|rds|aurora|azure|gcp|vercel|netlify|heroku|docker|kubernetes|graphql|trpc|playwright|cypress|puppeteer|selenium|websockets?|socket\.io|server-sent events|passkeys?|magic[ -]links?|sso|single sign-on|mfa|2fa|two-factor|oauth|oidc|saml)\b"
m = sorted({y.group(0).lower() for y in re.finditer(bad, x, re.I)}); assert not m, m
'

python3 -c 'import re, json, subprocess; t = open("docs/architecture.md", encoding="utf-8").read(); R = t.splitlines(); sec = {}; cur = None; fence = False; H = []
for i, l in enumerate(R):
    if l.startswith("```"): fence = not fence
    if not fence and re.match(r"#{1,6} ", l): H.append(i)
    if not fence and l.startswith("## "): cur = l[3:]; sec[cur] = []
    elif cur: sec[cur].append(l)
body = lambda s: "\n".join(sec[s])
bullets = lambda s: [l for l in sec[s] if re.match(r"([-*]|\d+\.) ", l)]
rows = [[c.strip() for c in l.strip().strip("|").split("|")] for l in sec["Dependencies"] if l.startswith("| `")]
pat = r"`(@?[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*(/[a-z0-9._-]+)?)`"
assert all(len(r) == 3 and re.fullmatch(pat, r[0]) for r in rows), ("one package per row, in backticks, with Package, Purpose, Decision", rows)
names = [re.fullmatch(pat, r[0]).group(1) for r in rows]; assert len(names) <= 8 and len(set(names)) == len(names), names
assert all(re.search(r"\bAD-\d{2}\b", r[2]) for r in rows), "each dependency names a decision"
pj = json.load(open("package.json")); have = set(pj.get("dependencies", {})) | set(pj.get("devDependencies", {})); assert not set(names) & have, ("already in package.json", sorted(set(names) & have))
for p in names: assert subprocess.run(["npm", "view", p, "name"], capture_output=True).returncode == 0, ("not on the npm registry", p)
'
